nodes.title: Degree-one Picard–Kummer and Gysin comparison
nodes.statement: For a smooth proper geometrically connected curve C/L of characteristic zero with L-rational basepoint and J=Pic0(C), let D=sum_s n_s[s] be a Galois-stable degree-zero divisor. Under J[p^a]=H1_et(C_bar,mu_p^a), the finite Gysin extension boundary associated to (n_s mod p^a)_s equals the Kummer cocycle of [O(D)] in H1(L,J[p^a]), with Gysin and connecting homomorphisms normalized by sigma(Q)−Q for p^a Q=[D]. Passing compatibly in a and then rationalizing identifies GH.1 AJ_et(D) with kappa_J([D]) in H1(L,V_pJ). For an actual quotient q:J→E this gives q_* AJ_et(D)=kappa_E(q[D]).
hypotheses: D is defined over L, or its finite support is treated as a Galois set; the support degree map includes residue degrees. Normalize the Poincare bundle at the basepoint and use the same Weil-pairing/Tate-twist convention in both exact sequences.

J and q are the actual Picard variety and modular quotient supplied by the curve/Jacobian owners. Continuous inverse limits require their cochain/derived-limit comparison; only the rational comparison is asserted before lattice bounds.
proofSteps: Choose a p^a-division line bundle M with M^(p^a)=O(D), and a trivialization on U=C minus support(D). Compute sigma(M)/M and the change of trivialization; the resulting cocycle is sigma(Q)−Q in Pic0[p^a].
Compare this cocycle with the extension obtained from the residue/Gysin sequence of U, retaining its degree-zero kernel and the same sign. Changing M or trivialization changes it by a coboundary.
Check transitions a+1→a, Galois descent and rational-equivalence independence; use the continuous comparison to pass to TpJ. Apply multiplication/Kummer naturality for q.

nodes.title: Uniform integral transport on the selected newform factor
nodes.statement: For the multiplicity-one f-factor selected in H1_et(C_bar,Qp) and its actual modular-quotient realization V, choose stable lattices T and Tprime. Construct Galois-equivariant integral maps a:T→Tprime and b:Tprime→T and a single nonzero d in O with ba=d id_T and ab=d id_Tprime. The maps induced on H1(E,−) for every finite ring-class E commute with restriction and corestriction, with the same d for all E. Consequently each induced kernel and cokernel, and their coherent inverse-limit versions, is annihilated by d. This asserts a bounded integral comparison, not an integral isomorphism unless d is a unit.
hypotheses: The chosen rational coefficient map is an isomorphism on this f-factor; no reverse identity on the whole Jacobian is claimed. The lattices are finite free over the same complete DVR after a fixed coefficient extension.
Track the auxiliary fine-level degree, rational idempotent denominator and modular quotient isogeny/congruence denominator in d. None may depend on the ring-class level.
proofSteps: Import the rational selected-factor map from AGR and the modular quotient. In fixed finite lattice bases clear denominators of this map and its inverse once; multiply the clearing scalars to obtain d and the two integral maps.
Galois equivariance passes to continuous cochain complexes; naturality gives restriction/corestriction commutativity at every field.
Apply the two composite identities on cochains, then cohomology. In inverse limits use the compatible reverse map to lift d times a coherent class; no right-exactness of inverse limit is assumed.

nodes.title: Local degree-one comparison over conductor fields
nodes.statement: For every finite extension E/L_v in the ring-class tower, including ramified E, and every E-rational degree-zero divisor D on the good-reduction curve, the Picard–Kummer/Gysin comparison over E agrees with the Bloch–Kato logarithm after the canonical map D_dR,Lv(V) tensor E ≅ D_dR,E(V). Pairing with the quotient differential satisfies log_E(q_*AJ_et,E(D))(omega_E)=c_pi AJ_dR,E(D)(omega_f) when pi*omega_E=c_pi omega_f. Restriction on finite local cohomology commutes with scalar extension of log, and corestriction is adjoint to field trace under this pairing.
hypotheses: Good reduction/de Rham and the actual H1_f logarithm domain are retained. An E-rational divisor need not descend to Lv. The BDP13 finite-unramified F comparison is used only with its own model hypotheses; it is not invoked over arbitrary ramified E without the local comparison theorem.
The quotient map, comparison isomorphisms, filtration quotient and differential functional are fixed geometrically, not by an arbitrary nonzero linear functional.
proofSteps: Apply the finite Picard–Kummer comparison over E itself and the supplier Bloch–Kato/crystalline comparison in the degree-one good-reduction range.
Use functoriality for q and the equality of pulled-back differentials to compute the scalar c_pi.
Prove restriction/log and corestriction/trace squares on the cochain/comparison maps, then check their pairings before taking any tower limit.

nodes.title: Finite-character moments and exact conductor
nodes.statement: Retain G_n=Gal(K_c0p^n/K) and its finite class component. For an O-valued finite-order character chi of exact last conductor n, the continuous Shapiro evaluation of the integral inverse-limit class is the descent of alpha^−n sum_{g in G_n} chi(g) z_n^g in the specified chi^−1 coefficient convention. If H_n is the last conductor kernel and the restricted lower class is H_n-invariant, the weighted lower term of z_n−(p^(2r−2)/alpha) res(z_n−1) at weight 2r vanishes when chi|H_n is nontrivial. No cancellation of a nonzero scalar in a torsion cohomology module is used. Finite-component traces and unit indices remain explicit.
hypotheses: Choose coefficients containing all chi values and the fixed Shapiro inversion convention; exact conductor means nonfactorization through G_n−1, as supplied by HE.0.

The stable integral system, bottom normalization and coefficient projections already exist. Use the actual quotient action, restriction and twisted descent, not a formal group sum in an unrelated module.
proofSteps: Apply the Iwasawa Shapiro map and evaluate the coefficient character on continuous cochains; compare the finite quotient formula with the unnormalized weighted class.
Use the ring-class conductor kernel theorem to translate exact conductor into nontriviality on H_n; prove the lower restriction image is H_n-fixed by restriction naturality.
Sum over H_n cosets. Apply existing scalar character orthogonality in an integral-domain coefficient ring and only then let the zero scalar act on the possibly torsion module.

Use the geometric pullback pi*omega_E=c_pi omega_f and the CM generator identity CH (5.3) to compute the scalar functional, without selecting a new arbitrary basis to force equality.

nodes.title: Ordinary-line application of regulator quotient descent
nodes.statement: For the actual critically twisted ordinary line F+Tdagger tensor xi^−1, verify the hypotheses of the requested local Part II and construct the anticyclotomic quotient regulator in the source completion. If q_M and q_N are the actual source/target quotient maps and Ltilde is the two-variable regulator, prove Ltilde^−1(ker q_N)=ker q_M before claiming injectivity of the descended map. Verify H0 of the tower ordinary line vanishes in the source’s range, hence the required H2 correction, and prove the canonical omega_family pairing is nonzero on its rank-one period line after scalar extension. Retain J, lambda localization and the pseudo-null error.
hypotheses: This is the GH application of proposed PHR2.1–PHR2.5, not a second construction of local Iwasawa theory. LZ14 injectivity before quotient and a generic mapQ lemma alone do not provide the arithmetic preimage equality.

The rank-one line has the exact unramified character Psi after all twists. Verify nonnegative Hodge–Tate, no trivial quotient and no tower invariants before using CH5.1; the p-old condition is required for Castella Corollary 3.9.
proofSteps: Identify the actual coefficient and distribution quotient submodules and their pushforwards from the supplied local regulator. Use the Galois-cohomology specialization sequence to compute the H2 error.

Prove the preimage equality, then apply the existing Mathlib quotient kernel formula. Pair only after proving a nonzero functional on a specified one-dimensional period line; a scalar projection on a rank-two space is insufficient.

Check interpolation at nonexceptional arithmetic points and the domain of each coefficient map. If nu(lambda)=0, construct and prove a regular model/cleared-denominator moment as a separate obligation; never evaluate lambda^−1 there.

Relative Lubin–Tate comparison and quotient correction.
Injectivity requires the infinite unramified direction; quotient injectivity needs the additional preimage calculation.

acceptance: Multiplication by X is injective on Q[X] but induces zero on Q[X]/(X); this rejects passing injectivity through a quotient. A nonzero functional on an identified line is injective, whereas a projection Q^2→Q is not.

nodes.title: Localization injectivity at weight-two p-old points
nodes.statement: In the common all-split CH/ordinary-family range, extend the localization comparison used in Castella Remark 6.6 to a weight-two p-old specialization: on each retained finite ring-class component, the strict Greenberg global Iwasawa Selmer module maps injectively to the ordinary local H1_Iw module. Together with source-period-and-twist-transport and ordinary-regulator-quotient-application this permits equality of local reciprocity images to identify the global p-old cycle/point class.
hypotheses: Residual restriction to G_K irreducible, p-distinguished ordinary representation, the actual torsion-free Greenberg module/control statements, infinitely many nonzero specialized local classes and their rank-one Selmer bounds. Retain E(K)[p]=0 when importing the HE.8 integral point system.
The form is p-old of level prime to p. No conclusion for the multiplicative p-new weight-two point or an exceptional lambda-zero specialization is asserted.
proofSteps: Repeat the argument of Castella Lemma 6.4 on each finite ring-class component using the weight-two CH nonvanishing and rank-one specialization theorem with their own hypotheses.
Use torsion freeness/control to deduce the global kernel vanishes from the characterwise vanishing; retain bad-prime local errors.
Apply the already constructed regulator and period diagrams. The additional infinite-unramified quotient check is independent of this global localization argument.

sources.locator: §6.2, Lemma 6.4 and proof, p.27; Remark 6.6, pp.28–29
sources.match: The proof route for the weight-two p-old extension; all hypotheses must be transported.

acceptance: A p-new multiplicative elliptic specialization fails the p-old input. Equality of two local images without the injectivity theorem cannot imply equality of global classes.

nodes.title: Hsieh nonvanishing hypothesis transport
nodes.statement: In the F=Q, all-split tame-level CH setup with (N_f,D_K)=1, choose an auxiliary coefficient prime ell different from the anticyclotomic tower prime p. Translate Hsieh14 Theorem C to nonzero central values modulo ell for all but finitely many p-power characters, then use the imported L3h interpolation to show the bounded p-adic square-root measure is nonzero. Nonzero bounded one-variable power series has only finitely many torsion-character zeros. This supplies GH.6 nonvanishing with its extra discriminant-level hypothesis.
hypotheses: Hsieh Theorem C: ordinary CM type at the coefficient prime, square-free nonsplit conductor n−, Hypothesis A epsilon*=+1 at v|n−, coprimality of coefficient/tower primes with n c_chi D_K, absolutely irreducible residual restriction to G_K and coefficient prime not dividing the specified local finite character orders.

For the CH all-split specialization n−=1, Hypothesis A and square-free n− hold automatically. Choose ell outside pND_K and the finite factors at nonsplit character conductor (including 1+q as in the CH proof), with the CM type ell-ordinary and the required residual irreducibility; this prime-existence input is part of the L3h request. Hsieh’s coefficient prime and tower prime are switched; the conclusion is not a mod-p claim for the original fixed form.
proofSteps: Read the Theorem C package with the roles of p and ell renamed before specializing F=Q. In local-degree one its almost-all conclusion means a finite exceptional set.
Check each local root-number, conductor and residual condition under the CH auxiliary-prime choice, rather than applying a bare nonvanishing citation.
Transport the algebraic central values through the L3h period/Euler interpolation, conclude nonidentity of the p-adic measure, and apply the existing Weierstrass-preparation supplier.

sources.locator: Introduction, Hypothesis A and (ord), pp.710–711; Theorem C, p.713; Theorem 7.1 and proof, pp.759–764
sources.match: Full nonvanishing package, including local-degree and auxiliary residual hypotheses.
Auxiliary-prime choice and switching the coefficient and tower primes.

acceptance: Nontriviality of a distribution alone does not establish a Selmer rank. In a multivariable or local-degree>1 tower, Theorem C does not assert a finite exceptional set; use its dense-set formulation instead.

nodes.title: Local conditions in the BSD auxiliary-form range
nodes.statement: Let g be an ordinary newform of weight k=2r≥2, p not dividing tame M, in exactly the ideal-Heegner/special-local range of Castella Birch erratum Theorem 2.3. Construct the graph/projected coefficient classes at this level and prove their stabilized/derived classes lie in the canonical self-dual Selmer local conditions: finite away from p except the specified transverse auxiliary condition, and the corrected finite/ordinary condition at p. The nonsplit tame primes permitted here are ramified in K and divide M exactly once; inert primes cannot satisfy O_K/mathfrak M ≅ Z/MZ. This theorem extends the all-split source range and is not an instance of CH (H).
hypotheses: p>3, p split in K, M≥3, ideal mathfrak M with O_K/mathfrak M ≅ Z/MZ; residual g|G_K irreducible; some nonsplit q exactly divides M; if 2 is nonsplit then 2 exactly divides M; at each nonsplit ell exactly dividing M, the source’s special representation is an unramified twist with ell sent to −ell^(r−1).

Keep all projector/lattice/integral-twist restrictions explicit. The condition p not dividing (2r−1)! cannot be imposed silently on unbounded congruence weights; either establish an integral construction without it or prove a source-valid replacement for the actual weight set.
proofSteps: Use BDP17 §4.1 ideal-Heegner CM level geometry, where ramified tame primes of exponent one are allowed, and the requested fine-level geometry/lattice interface. Construct actual integral coefficient maps and record denominators.

Extend the tame norm/Frobenius calculation at good auxiliary primes and compute the bad ramified-tame local condition using the stated special type and residual ramification/control; the all-split calculation is not treated as that proof.

Apply the CH erratum via KO20 Lemma 4.10 at p, verifying the integral Ω/twist hypotheses for this coefficient lattice and conductor field. The actual nonsplit local and unbounded-weight integral verifications are recorded source gaps.

sources.match: Precise auxiliary-form range and local theorem calls; does not independently prove the range extension.

nodes.title: Integral auxiliary-form Kolyvagin system and leading unit
nodes.statement: For each auxiliary g in auxiliary-form-local-range, construct its integral Lambda-adic Kolyvagin system from the actual stabilized generalized-cycle Iwasawa class kappa_g,infty. With the lattice, finite ring-class trace and Shapiro convention fixed, identify an explicit v_g in O_g^times with kappa_g,1=v_g kappa_g,infty and give v_g^−1. The local finite–singular correction factors u_ell are units; their empty product at n=1 is 1. A fixed nonzero denominator d_g or a rational isomorphism does not replace the leading unit.
hypotheses: All generic ES hypotheses needed for the chosen descent theorem are verified in this auxiliary range. LV16 admissibility is an all-split, exceptional-prime package and cannot be silently applied here.

The LV19 Theorem 4.7 invoked by the erratum must be collated in its version of record, or an independently applicable construction proved. Denominator and weight conditions are checked on the actual auxiliary forms, not assumed from the elliptic weight-two form.
proofSteps: Extend the integral norm-compatible class with the local conditions from auxiliary-form-local-range and import ES.3 derivative/descent machinery. Prove residual invariant vanishing and finite–singular compatibility for this representation.

Compute every coefficient, finite-component trace and tower-index normalization relating the leading derivative to kappa_g,infty. Apply inverse unit corrections at auxiliary primes; the empty-product normalization itself introduces no factor at n=1.

Collate LV19 Theorem 4.7 and its hypotheses against this construction. LV16 Theorem 4.7, pp.15–16, is a model for the correction calculation only; its hypotheses do not prove the nonsplit/varying-weight claim.

sources.match: Names LV19 Theorem 4.7 and the required initial unit comparison.
Verified v1 inverse correction factors and unchanged initial class, in its own admissible range only.

acceptance: Taking v_g=p is rejected even though it is nonzero rationally. At n=1 the correction unit product equals 1; any extra initial scalar must come from an explicitly computed tower/lattice map.

nodes.title: Non-torsion in the auxiliary-form source range
nodes.statement: For g in auxiliary-form-local-range, prove kappa_g,infty is non-torsion over the specified anticyclotomic Iwasawa algebra. Realize the square-root analytic distribution in the same coefficient/twist convention, prove its nonvanishing with the local-root-number/conductor conditions at ramified tame primes, and prove the source-qualified reciprocity formula on the integral class. For a nonzero scalar functional of the localized class, conclude the class is nonzero; use the established torsion-free Selmer/Iwasawa module to obtain non-torsion.
hypotheses: The special nonsplit local types of the erratum and all residual/ordinary assumptions are retained. CH Theorem 3.9 has the extra (N_f,D_K)=1 and cannot prove this ramified-tame extension. Hsieh Hypothesis A is a local sign condition to verify here, not automatically vacuous.

The regulator map is defined at the selected nonexceptional specializations; period/Euler factors are nonzero. Exceptional multiplicative specialization is an analytic regular-model problem in the consumer route, not a p-old class theorem.
proofSteps: Request from L3h Hsieh Theorem C/interpolation with exact special-local test-vector and sign checks at the ramified tame primes of the auxiliary form.

Extend the generalized-cycle reciprocity calculation in GH.4 to the same source range using the local range theorem and the fixed regulator/twist maps; do not use all-split CH5.7 without this adapter.

Combine analytic nonvanishing and the nonzero-line regulator pairing with torsion freeness of the actual global module. This is the non-torsion input used by the corrected BSD proof; the source-range reciprocity verification remains explicit.

Supply the source-qualified higher-weight scalar reciprocity identity and native Castella analytic moments in coefficient models where reduction modulo p^m is defined. Record the precise allowed weight set and all denominators; an unbounded sequence cannot satisfy a fixed-p factorial exclusion. At a lambda-zero multiplicative point construct the required analytic regular model/cleared-denominator specialization, rather than applying the p-old cycle comparison. This adapter is the exact GH input to BSD.6a; BSD owns coefficient congruences, characteristic-ideal/control comparison and the limit argument.
hypotheses: Theorem 2.3’s ideal Heegner, special nonsplit local types, condition at 2, split p and residual irreducibility hold for each g_m. The consumer supplies the actual congruence sequence and lattices, not arbitrary weight specializations.

The new auxiliary local/system/non-torsion theorem targets and regular analytic model are proved before this export is applied. These remain explicit gaps in this plan; the erratum’s conclusion is not assumed as their proof.
proofSteps: Identify the class in the three auxiliary targets with the source’s Section 5.2 stabilized class through exact lattice/tower maps and the computed unit v_g.

Prove the corresponding nonsplit-range scalar reciprocity comparison and identify its distribution with the native Castella analytic moment in a regular coefficient model; retain all unit, sign, period and finite-component maps.

Apply the defined reduction maps to the exact equalities. Hand the resulting identities and unit inverses to BSD.6a, which performs the congruence/control transfer to the p-new multiplicative elliptic form.
